ev.q: The rate of 1.5 TB cases per 100,000 population among U.S.-born persons represented a 10.3% decrease since 2010
Provisional 2011 surveillance data indicate a TB case rate of 3.4 cases per 100,000 persons
In 2011, a total of 10,521 new tuberculosis (TB) cases were reported in the United States, an incidence of 3.4 cases per 100,000 population
Among persons with TB, 95.4% of Asians, 73.9% of Hispanics, 36.4% of blacks, and 20.9% of whites were foreign-born.
The 17.3 per 100,000 population TB rate among foreign-born persons was a 4.8% decrease since 2010
From 2010 to 2011, TB rates decreased most for blacks, then Hispanics, whites, and Asians.
Among U.S.-born racial and ethnic groups, the greatest racial disparity in TB rates occurred among non-Hispanic blacks
This report summarizes 2011 TB surveillance data reported to CDC's National Tuberculosis Surveillance System.
The percentage decline is greater than the average 3.8% decline per year observed from 2000 to 2008
falls short of the 2010 goal of TB elimination (less than one case per 1,000,000)

methods_quotes.q: CDC calculates national and state TB rates overall and by racial/ethnic group, using U.S. Census Bureau population estimates
therefore, 2010 population estimates were used as denominators to calculate 2011 case rates.
Because 2011 Current Population Survey data were available, 2011 population estimates were used for U.S.-born and foreign-born TB rates.
Population figures from 2010 were used to calculate 2010 and 2011 rates.
